title: Perf-canary: add cache-heavy scenario to validate KV/prefix cache hit-rate stability across runtime releases
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Add a cache-heavy perf-canary benchmark scenario that (a) exercises prefix/KV cache behavior deterministically and (b) detects regressions in cache hit-rate and realized latency savings across runtime releases.

Why
We’re upgrading cache telemetry to v2 and changing instrumentation paths. We need a safety net that runs on every runtime train to catch:
- hit-rate drops caused by cache lookup/insert/evict regressions
- misclassification changes (hit/miss/partial)
- silent changes that keep hit-rate stable but reduce realized savings (e.g., prefill reuse broken)

Scope
- Add a new perf-canary scenario "cache_prefix_stability_v1" that generates a controlled mix of:
  1) high-reuse prompts (stable shared prefix) -> should produce high hit-rate
  2) moderate-reuse prompts (prefix bucketed / slight variations) -> should produce stable partial hit-rate
  3) low-reuse prompts (random prefix) -> should produce near-zero hit-rate
- Run scenario on at least 2 sequence-length distributions to ensure behavior doesn’t drift with longer prompts.
- Collect v2 cache metrics (or interim compatibility mapping if v2 not fully rolled out) and compute:
  - cache_hit_rate = hits / (hits + misses) with partial handled per spec
  - hit_bytes and saved_prefill_ms (if available from runtime build) for sanity correlation
- Add regression thresholds + gating behavior:
  - warn-only initially for 1 runtime cycle
  - then convert to release gating for the runtime train once signal is stable

Non-goals
- Validating customer-specific routing/cardinality behaviors (this is synthetic + controlled)
- Catching all caching algorithm changes (we’re focusing on hit-rate stability and gross savings deltas)

Implementation notes
- Determinism: use fixed RNG seed, fixed prompt corpus checked into perf-canary repo, and a fixed request schedule.
- Warm-up: include an explicit warm-up phase (e.g., 50 requests) before measuring, to avoid false failures due to cold cache.
- Isolation: run with a dedicated synthetic tenant/route in perf-canary to avoid interference from other scenarios.
- Runtime config: enable prefix/KV cache explicitly and pin cache policy settings (capacity, eviction policy) in the scenario config so defaults don’t change under us.

Metrics/Signals
Primary (gating):
- Hit-rate (high-reuse cohort): must be >= baseline - 3pp AND >= 0.70 (exact baseline will be set after 3 green runs)
- Hit-rate (low-reuse cohort): must be <= 0.05 (detects accidental over-counting / misclassification)
Secondary (alert-only):
- saved_prefill_ms per request: must not drop by >15% vs baseline when high-reuse hit-rate is stable
- p95 prefill latency: must not regress by >10% vs baseline for the high-reuse cohort

Acceptance criteria
- New scenario lands in perf-canary with docs describing how it works and what it catches.
- CI runs the scenario on the standard GPU matrix used for runtime train qualification (at minimum: 1 mainstream SKU).
- Scenario exports a single summary artifact per run containing cohort-level counters and computed hit-rates.
- Regression detection is wired into the existing runtime release workflow (initially warn-only; follow-up to gate after one cycle).
- False-positive rate is acceptable: no more than 1 spurious failure across 10 consecutive nightly runs.

Links / related work
- Linear umbrella: ENG-4812 (Cache hit-rate instrumentation sprint)
- Runtime instrumentation: ENG-4813, ENG-4814
- Telemetry pipeline changes: ENG-4815
- Perf-canary PR (target): sources/github/perf-canary/pr-233.json
- Profiling/overhead guide (reference): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/cache-telemetry-overhead-profiling-guide.json

Open questions
- Which metric names are stable for canary consumption during the v1->v2 migration window (temporary mapping vs hard switch)?
- Should partial hits count as hits for the high-reuse cohort gate, or should we gate on (hit + partial) separately to detect shifts in classification?

Plan
1) Draft scenario config + prompt corpus
2) Implement metrics extraction + summary artifact
3) Run locally against runtime main and capture initial baseline
4) Land warn-only thresholds, let it bake for ~1 week
5) Promote to gating once the baseline/variance is understood
comments: 2025-02-12 (Marcus Reed): Drafted initial scenario design: 3 cohorts (high/moderate/low reuse) with fixed prompt corpus + seed. Need confirmation from Logan/Omar on which counters are stable to consume while v2 rolls out.

2025-02-13 (Logan Wright): Prefer using the v2 aggregate counters where available; during migration window, OK to map legacy counters -> v2 equivalents as long as the scenario output includes both raw counters and computed rates. Please keep cohort labels low-cardinality and fixed.

2025-02-17 (Omar El-Sayed): Partial-prefill counting is still being tuned. For gating, recommend: (1) gate on (hit + partial) rate for the high-reuse cohort, and (2) separately track strict-hit rate as a secondary signal until classification is stable.

2025-02-19 (Marcus Reed): Implemented warm-up phase and cohort tagging in scenario runner; working on summary artifact format. Noted that cache warm-up needs to be explicit per model load to avoid cross-test contamination.

2025-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE POV: start warn-only, and only gate once we have a week of variance data. Add a clear failure message pointing to the cache telemetry data quality runbook if counters are missing/zero.

2025-02-24 (Marcus Reed): Baseline run on runtime-1.18.0-rc1 looks stable for high/low cohorts. Moderate cohort variance higher than expected; suspect prompt set includes too much prefix diversity. Will refine corpus and rerun before setting thresholds.
